html:
SMTO-FIL-0052 — The drive you chose is no longer available

GUID: f1e6c753-6b9d-41a6-8cc9-3d1e351ea63d
Slug: removable-destination-unavailable
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: fil

What happened

  • SMTO can't find the USB or external drive you picked earlier, or it was unplugged and plugged back in. SMTO didn't write anything in this step.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Plug the same drive back into the computer running the Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses on that computer) and wait until it shows up there. SMTO only writes to the exact drive you chose, and checks that it is really connected first.
  2. If SMTO asks you to choose a drive, reply with its number or folder path from the list it shows. SMTO checks your answer against the drives connected right now.
  3. If it still says the drive is unavailable after you reconnected it, start a new conversation and name the drive's folder in your request, or name a different drive. Reconnecting gives the drive a new identity, and SMTO won't reuse the old choice for it in this conversation.
  4. Before redoing the copy, ask SMTO to list what is already on the drive. Files from earlier steps may have been saved before the drive went away.

What success looks like

  • SMTO saves to the drive without this message, and the files appear on it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't assume nothing was copied earlier just because the drive disappeared; check the drive first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The removable-destination guard could not re-observe the bound volume: it is missing from the Gateway's current inventory, its volume identity changed, or a resumed choice no longer matches; no write was started.

What this means

  • A selected removable path/volume no longer matches current inventory, its bound identity changed, or resume cannot re-observe the selected choice. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • A selected removable path/volume no longer matches current inventory, its bound identity changed, or resume cannot re-observe the selected choice.

How to diagnose it

  • Recheck the exact selected device/mount and current inventory; the rejected step has not started its write.

How to fix it

  • Compare the binding under removable_destination_resolution with the Gateway's current removable_destinations inventory (mount_point, device, volume_id); volume_id includes the device node's ctime, so a replug changes it. Remount the same device or have the user explicitly select a destination; a stale binding for the same mount point persists within the conversation, so a new conversation clears it.
  • Reconnect that exact drive and identify its mount path, or explicitly select another eligible destination.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The same intended eligible volume is revalidated or another destination is explicitly selected.

What not to do

  • Do not treat a lost connection as proof that earlier remote work did not run.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
